questions.q: Which statement about a vendor demo is true?
options: It is not an evaluation; test on your golden set with baselines
why: Not always, but it is not evidence for your data.

questions.q: An API costs 1.20 per 1,000 forecasts with no fixed cost. What is the monthly cost for 5 million forecasts?
Scenario: latency must be under 100 ms and the API takes 400 ms. What do you do first?
options: Remove the API from the options
Compare cost for the API anyway
why: Correct: hard limits filter options before cost comparison.
A cheaper but infeasible option is useless.
A hard limit cannot be ignored.

questions.q: Why include seasonal naive in the evaluation of a foundation model?
options: To check that the model is worth its cost over a free baseline
It is required by the vendor

questions.q: Scenario: the vendor changes its model version and your forecasts shift. Which measure would have helped?
options: Pinning versions and keeping an evaluation that runs on each update
why: Correct: you detect and control changes.

questions.q: What is a sensible exit plan for a vendor?
options: Own your data and golden evaluation, use an adapter, keep a fallback model, estimate exit cost

questions.q: Scenario: you have rich known-future features (price, promotions) driving demand. A zero-shot model that ignores them will likely:
options: Beat your tuned model by a lot
Lose to a model that uses those features, unless it supports covariates
why: Without the key drivers it often loses.
Correct: check covariate support and test it.
